chapter: New York sessions: Sinatra, Miles, Birth of the Cool
title: Lost tape and John Lewis's Toccata
summary: After a tape gap, he says John Lewis's Toccata showed him Lewis was drawn to other musical worlds, leading to their Third Stream work.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis
story.community_name: Playing with Miles Davis: joining, sessions and the band

blocks.x: [The first half hour of tape 2 (disc 2) was lost, for reasons unknown. The recording resumes in the midst of a discussion of John Lewis.]

I could tell by the touch that this was not just some jazz player. He was into other worlds of music. When I saw that he had written a piece called Toccata – that’s the first time anybody took an Italian form of music with a particular concept to it and used it in a jazz context. So I knew that he was interested in more. The rest is history. We went together, and he and I created this whole Third Stream thing.
